The answer is B. The statute only bars force in resisting an arrest, and it doesn't remove the right to defend against excessive force. On the suspect's account, the officer began beating him with a nightstick over mere cursing, so his punch was self-defense and he should be acquitted if the jury believes that account. The team note has it backwards: an unlawful arrest doesn't strip a person of the privilege to use force. If anything, it makes resistance more defensible, so D is wrong.

CONFIDENCE: 85
